note: priority 1 = life-safety / special-needs steps, surfaced ahead of general steps. See scoring.rank_next_steps.

steps.title: Make a backup power plan for medical equipment
how_to: List every device that needs electricity and how long its battery lasts.
Ask the equipment supplier what backup options they support.
Decide where you would go if the power stays off, and how you would get there.
Tell your utility you have a power-dependent medical need and ask about their medical-needs register.

self_check.label: I know what we would do if the power went out for 24 hours

steps.title: Do a 7-day medication check
how_to: Write down every daily medication for each person.
Count how many days of each you have on hand right now.
Ask your doctor or pharmacist how to build up to a 7-day supply and how to rotate it.
Keep the written list with your emergency documents.

self_check.label: We have about a week of each daily medication, and a written list

steps.medical_note: Not medical advice. Ask your doctor or pharmacist about medications and medical devices.

steps.title: Make a transportation plan
how_to: Decide who would drive you, or which transit or paratransit service you would use.
Agree a backup in case your first choice is not available.
Save their numbers in your phone and write them on the family plan.

self_check.label: We know how we would physically leave, and who would drive

steps.title: Arrange someone to help you evacuate
how_to: Ask one specific neighbour, friend or relative to be your evacuation helper, and agree a backup.
Give them a key or tell them how they would get in.
Agree how they will reach you if phones are down.

self_check.label: A specific person has agreed to help us leave, and we have a backup

steps.title: Put together an infant feeding kit
how_to: Work through CDC's emergency infant-feeding checklist for how your baby is fed.
Store clean water for preparing feeds and for cleaning feeding equipment.
Keep enough feeding supplies for several days and check expiry dates when the clocks change.

self_check.label: We have several days of feeding supplies and a way to clean them

steps.title: Make a written family emergency plan
how_to: Agree where you will meet if you cannot get home, and a second place outside the neighbourhood.
Pick one out-of-area contact everybody can call, since local lines are often busy.
Write it on one page, photograph it, and give a copy to each adult.

self_check.label: Our plan is written down somewhere everyone can find

steps.title: Build your kit in phases (water and light first)
how_to: Phase 1: water, one gallon per person per day for three days, plus a flashlight and batteries.
Phase 2: three days of food that needs no cooking, and a radio.
Phase 3: a first-aid kit and a way to charge your phone.
Add a little each shop rather than buying it all at once.

self_check.label: Three days of water per person
Three days of food that needs no cooking
A way to charge a phone with the power off

steps.title: Make a pet go-kit and find pet-friendly lodging
how_to: Pack several days of pet food and water, a spare leash or carrier, and any pet medication.
Add a copy of vaccination records and a photo of you with your pet in case you are separated.
Call two places outside your area now and check they take pets in an emergency.

self_check.label: A go-kit is packed for every pet
We know somewhere pet-friendly we could go

steps.title: Learn your evacuation routes
how_to: Find two different ways out of your neighbourhood.
Drive or walk each one once so it is familiar.
Write both on the family plan.

self_check.label: We know two ways out of our neighbourhood

steps.title: Turn on emergency alerts
how_to: Check Wireless Emergency Alerts are on in your phone settings.
Sign up for your county or city alert service.
Consider a NOAA Weather Radio if you lose signal where you live.

self_check.label: Emergency alerts are switched on for every phone in the house
